==Problem==
Qiang drives <imath>15</imath> miles at an average speed of <imath>30</imath> miles per hour. How many additional miles will he have to drive at <imath>55</imath> miles per hour to average <imath>50</imath> miles per hour for the entire trip?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }45\qquad\textbf{(B) }62\qquad\textbf{(C) }90\qquad\textbf{(D) }110\qquad\textbf{(E) }135</imath>

==Solution 1 (by looking at the answer choices)==
The only option that is easily divisible by <imath>55</imath> is <imath>110</imath>, which gives 2 hours of travel. And, the formula is <imath>\frac{15}{30} + \frac{110}{55} = \frac{5}{2}</imath>.

And, <imath>\text{Average Speed}</imath> = <imath>\frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}</imath>.
 
Thus, <imath>\frac{125}{50} = \frac{5}{2}</imath>.

Both are equal and thus our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 110}.</imath>

==Solution 2==
To calculate the average speed, simply evaluate the total distance over the total time. Let the number of additional miles he has to drive be <imath>x.</imath> Therefore, the total distance is <imath>15+x</imath> and the total time (in hours) is <cmath>\frac{15}{30}+\frac{x}{55}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{x}{55}.</cmath> We can set up the following equation: <cmath>\frac{15+x}{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{x}{55}}=50.</cmath> Simplifying the equation, we get <cmath>15+x=25+\frac{10x}{11}.</cmath> Solving the equation yields <imath>x=110,</imath> so our answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 110}</imath>.

==Solution 3==
If he travels <imath>15</imath> miles at a speed of <imath>30</imath> miles per hour, he travels for 30 min. Average rate is total distance over total time so <imath>(15+d)/(0.5 + t) = 50</imath>, where d is the distance left to travel and t is the time to travel that distance. Solve for <imath>d</imath> to get <imath>d = 10+50t</imath>. You also know that he has to travel <imath>55</imath> miles per hour for some time, so <imath>d=55t</imath>. Plug that in for d to get <imath>55t = 10+50t</imath> and <imath>t=2</imath> and since <imath>d=55t</imath>, <imath>d = 2\cdot55 =110</imath>, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 110}</imath>.

==Solution 4== 

Let <imath>h</imath> be the amount of hours Qiang drives after his first 15 miles. Average speed, which we know is <imath>50</imath> mph, means total distance over total time. For 15 miles at 30 mph, the time taken is <imath>\frac{1}{2}</imath> hour, so the total time for this trip would be <imath>\frac{1}{2} + h</imath> hours. For the total distance, 15 miles are traveled in the first part and <imath>55h</imath> miles in the second. This gives the following equation: 


<cmath>\dfrac{15+55h}{\frac{1}{2}+h} = 50.</cmath> 




Cross multiplying, we get that <imath>15 + 55h = 50h + 25</imath>, and simple algebra gives <imath>h=2</imath>. In 2 hours traveling at 55 mph, the distance traveled is <imath>\frac{2 \hspace{0.05 in} \text{hours}}{1} \cdot \frac{55 \hspace{0.05 in} \text{miles}}{1 \hspace{0.05 in} \text{hour}} = 2 \cdot 55 \hspace{0.05 in} \text{miles} = 110 \hspace{0.05 in} \text{miles}</imath>, which is choice <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 110}</imath>. 




~TaeKim
